title: 485 Huron Road redevelopment approved at special meeting
subtitle: Older adult online programming agreement, new councillor's committee appointments, and remembrance of the Quebec City Mosque attack.
overview: Council met in a short special session and approved an Official Plan amendment and a zoning by-law amendment for 485 Huron Road, requested by Activa Holdings Inc. {{vote:m2}}. The official plan change goes to the Region of Waterloo for approval. The related by-laws were added to the agenda and given third reading the same day, so the zoning change takes effect without waiting for another meeting.

Council also authorized an agreement with The Jewish Home for the Aged for a web-based platform for online older adult programming, known as Baycrest@Home {{vote:m1}}. The aim is to improve the quality of life of older adults.

Councillor Stephanie Stretch, newly appointed to Ward 10, was named to the Downtown Action Advisory Committee, the Downtown Kitchener Business Improvement Area and the Climate Change and Environment Committee. These appointments had been deferred from January 8. Council opened by marking the National Day of Remembrance of the Quebec City Mosque Attack, and later met in-camera on a land matter {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.detail: Council adopted the Official Plan amendment for Special Policy Area 41, to be forwarded to the Region of Waterloo for approval, and approved the zoning by-law amendment for Activa Holdings Inc.

The General Manager of Community Services and Deputy CAO was authorized to sign an agreement with The Jewish Home for the Aged for a web-based platform serving older adults, to the City Solicitor's satisfaction.
Council authorized a closed meeting after the special meeting to consider a land acquisition or disposition matter under the Municipal Act.

debate: There was no recorded debate on the main items: the older adult programming report and the 485 Huron Road applications were each moved and carried after the chair asked for discussion.
No delegations were registered, so the meeting included no public input on the planning application beyond any written comments circulated to council.

Two councillors declared conflicts of interest on part of a land matter on the closed-session agenda, one because of employment and one because of family property near the subject, and did not take part in that item.
The mayor's remembrance statement described a rise in Islamophobia and urged residents to join the Green Square campaign.
